pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.originalLogic: GVN's `try_as_place` reconstructs a MIR `Place` from a value-graph index. After walking an existing `projection` and failing to recover a local, it can encounter `Value::Projection(pointer, proj)` and recursively extend the projection, returning `Some(place)` once the accumulated projection is materialized as `Place { local, projection: self.tcx.mk_place_elems(projection.as_slice()) }`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical behavior did not stop when the accumulated projection already ended in `PlaceElem::Deref` and no local had been found. It could continue into the `Value::Projection` extension path and append further projections, producing an ill-formed place rather than declining to produce one. The merged fix inserts an explicit guard that returns `None` in that state instead of extending the projection.
analysis.inputDomain: GVN-internal value/projection graphs during `try_as_place`, specifically an index whose reconstructed projection has `PlaceElem::Deref` as its last element while no local has been found, and where a subsequent `Value::Projection` would otherwise be appended. The PR reports triggering this condition via rust-lang/rust#143333, but the supplied material does not include the program itself.
analysis.summary: GVN's place reconstruction must not append projections after an already-terminal `Deref` when no local has been recovered. Doing so can create an ill-formed MIR place. The fix makes `try_as_place` return `None` in that case; the supplied patch contains only the compiler change, with no regression-test hunk.
analysis.trigger: `try_as_place` reaches the `else if projection.last() == Some(&PlaceElem::Deref)` state—i.e. a local was not found and the current projection already ends in `Deref`—while attempting to reconstruct a place through further `Value::Projection` values.
preconditions: GVN is running `try_as_place` on a value index.
The accumulated projection already ends with `PlaceElem::Deref`.
No local has been recovered for the place.
Without the guard, control would fall through to the `Value::Projection` extension branch.
pitfalls: Do not treat `Deref` as an ordinary projection that can be freely followed by additional projections during this reconstruction; the source states `Deref` can only be the first projection in a place.
Returning `Some(place)` with additional projections after `Deref` yields an ill-formed place, even if the value graph otherwise type-checks.
A retained test name or old comment does not prove the replacement pass behavior is correct; compare actual value assignments in decoded MIR revisions.
Borrowing restrictions and post-copy overwrites are separate conditions from this projection-order bug and should not be conflated with it.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct a focused GVN/MIR place-reconstruction scenario in which the reconstructed projection already ends in `Deref` and no local is found, then exercises a further `Value::Projection`. The two variants should differ only in whether that additional projection is requested: the corrected GVN behavior is `None` (no place), whereas the historical behavior would attempt to return a place with projections appended after `Deref`. Also inspect the decoded MIR diff by comparing actual value assignments per revision rather than relying on test names/comments. No compiler was built and no execution was performed for this analysis.
